thread.title: Tech Today: Defending Micron, Apple's Narrative, Can Tesla Make Cars?

author: Barron's
title: Tech Today: Defending Micron, Apple's Narrative, Can Tesla Make Cars?
text:
Here are some things going on today in the world of tech :
Can Tesla Make Cars? Shares of Tesla ( TSLA ) are up $4.01, or 1.4%, at $288.74, despite some continuing to ask whether the company can make cars successfully, a question that's dogged Tesla despite improving production rates.
Needham & Co. 's Rajvindra Gill started coverage of the stock with a Hold rating, after concluding the company won't make its targets for production of the Model 3 sedan, which was supposed to be 5,000 units built per month by the end of this month, which Tesla declared back on April 3 .
Instead, Gill thinks Tesla won't even make 2,500 on a "sustainable" basis" until the September quarter, and the 5,000 per month won't be hit until this time next year. "Our comprehensive checks on Model 3 production point to manufacturing problems, particularly at the battery cell level, module assembly and factory automation lines," writes Gill.
Gill also thinks Tesla's advantage over a longer period of time in things such as materials, cooling systems, and battery management, are going to "shrink."
Google's Waymo's Way Forward Speaking of automobiles, shares of Alphabet ( GOOGL ) are up $35.88, or 3.26%, to $1,135.88 after Google's Waymo self-driving unit today announced that Fiat Chrysler will add 62,000 more of the company's "Chrysler Pacifica Hybrid" minivans to Waymo's fleet of self-driving cars by the end of this year, and also how they can bring Waymo's self-driving-car technology to Chrysler cars.
In response, Morgan Stanley 's Brian Nowak this morning reiterates an Overweight rating on Alphabet stock, and a $1,200 price target, writing that the announcement is "another example of Waymo taking steps for how it could scale its self-driving fleet." He notes a prior deal to "add 20,000 all-electric Jaguar I-Pace SUVs" to the fleet. Nowak has a $75 billion estimated valuation for Waymo .
Just as important is monetization for Waymo. He notes that has been "a common question among investors," and he thinks "the potential of licensing revenue speaks to the opportunity for multiple revenue streams."
Defending Micron Shares of Micron Technology ( MU ) are up 96 cents, or 1.6%, at $58.55, after the stock yesterday fell about 8% on a downgrade by Joseph Moore at Morgan Stanley . Helping the stock today is a note from Mizuho 's Vijay Rakesh , who reiterates a Buy rating, and a $70 price target, writing that while prices of NAND chips are declining, demand continues to be robust, as it is for DRAM , whose prices also remain strong.
He points out Micron management's comments from the analyst day meeting last week. He notes that "average standard server content" of DRAM chips is going to 366 gigabytes by 2021 from 145 gigabytes in 2017.
And Micron "sees standard server content [of NAND] at ~11 terabytes by 2021, a 5-6x increase from 2017."
Furthermore, "We believe the 1xnm and 64L NAND transition and better NAND demand should continue to drive gross margin strength," writes Rakesh.
Apple's'Narrative' Another stock getting some defense this morning is Apple ( AAPL ). UBS's Steve Milunovich today reiterates a Buy rating, and raises his price target to $210 from $190, after surveying 6,700 smartphone users across five countries and seeing evidence that iPhone average selling prices remain "strong."
Milunovich thinks the more important point for Apple is that its "narrative" is shifting from just selling iPhones by the units to being more of a "consistent franchise," that is both hardware and software, according to a summary of the report by TheFlyontheWall .
Apple shares today are up $2.67, or 1.4%, at $189.54.
Zuora Soars, Workday Flops Among yesterday's earnings reports , the positive results for VMware ( VMW ), Zuora (ZUO), and Yext (YEXT), have driven their gains today well above the after-hours gains last night.
Zuora is up a whopping $3.80, or 17%, at $25.98, after its first quarterly report as a public company. VMware is up $8.02, or almost 6%, at $145.50, and Yext is up $1.11, or over 7%, at $16.50.
Still trading down, however is Workday (WDAY), the cloud- software darling, despite its beating fiscal Q1 expectations and slightly raising its revenue outlook. Its shares are down $5.03, or 3.8%, at $125.93.
The problem, according to Jefferies & Co .'s John DiFucci , was the " billings " number, which came in at $496 million, below the number the Street had been expecting, $519 million.
Also, he notes the company's outlook for its "short-term deferred revenue" is for 25% growth this quarter, which " implies a strong deceleration as Workday grew ST deferred revenue on average 32% through F2018."
The business "momentum is positive," for Workday, he concludes, but things are moving slowly.
